question: What changed in the latest Autodesk Fusion update?
answer:
Based on Autodesk Fusion's October 2026 major update (v.2706.1.14, October 21, 2026), followed by minor update v.2706.1.17 on October 28, 2026 [2].

- **Auto Timeline:** It uses AI-assisted feature reconstruction to turn imported, non-native geometry into an editable parametric design. It currently reconstructs extrudes, revolves, chamfers, fillets, holes and basic sweeps, and is meant for quick adjustments, not full rebuilds [3].
- **System Modeler:** This is a node-based, no-code environment for automating repetitive design and manufacturing tasks [3].
- **Performance:** Large, nested assemblies open, save and edit up to 35% faster. Legacy assemblies open up to 80% faster after a one-time override cleanup [2].
- **Autodesk Assistant and API:** The Assistant has better context awareness, and API coverage is broader [2].
- **Turning:** Updates include true fixture position after bar pull, cusp clearing and tool limits [3].
- **Electronics and drawings:** The eCAD drawings toolbar adds drill views, drill tables and copper views [3]. Polygon Pour is now called Copper Pour in Fusion Electronics, with a single fill-visibility toggle and clearer feedback when re-filling pours [2].
- **Data management:** Integrated task management adds Kanban and list views, and the Assistant can create or update tasks. Copy Designs Across Fusion Hubs is also new. Both are staged rollouts over about two weeks [2][3].
- **Minor update fixes:** v.2706.1.17 improves stability with inconsistent component data, decals and canvases, and fixes a blank Render workspace when a section analysis was active [2].

Fusion will require an Apple silicon Mac to stay up to date from the end of March 2027, after which Intel Macs get no updates or support [2].

keyPoints.text: The October 2026 Fusion update adds AI-assisted Auto Timeline that converts imported non-native geometry into an editable parametric design.
System Modeler is a new no-code, node-based automation environment for repetitive design and manufacturing tasks.
Performance improved, with up to 35% faster open, save and edit on large nested assemblies and up to 80% faster opening of legacy assemblies.
Built-in task management and new eCAD drawing views (drill views, drill tables, copper views) were added.

mayBeStale.text: Autodesk Fusion will require an Apple silicon Mac from end of March 2027, so Intel Mac support is ending.
Auto Timeline currently reconstructs only extrudes, revolves, chamfers, fillets, holes and basic sweeps, with more feature types promised later.
Task management is a staged rollout over two weeks, so it may not yet be available to every user.
Menu locations and feature availability (e.g., drill views under the drawings toolbar, copper views under the Create menu) are release-specific and may change.
